scope.label: Bronisław Kaper early career, documented through 1939

records.title: Ihre Majestät die Liebe
records.attributionNote: Kaper's participation in the German film record remains probable but functionally unresolved. The only positive trace currently documented in the database is IMDb/SRC0520, where he appears under the attested source form “Benjamin Kapper”. Filmportal/SRC0117 and Jurmann estate song-list evidence SRC0306 do not independently confirm Kaper and do not justify assigning an arranger or composer role as fact. Do not infer Kaper's participation mechanically from the confirmed Kaper involvement in the French-language version Son altesse l'amour (F005/W-F005).
records.publicNote: Bronisław Kaper’s involvement in this film is currently considered probable, but his role has not been established. The only positive attribution identified so far is IMDb, where he is listed as “Benjamin Kapper”; Filmportal and Walter Jurmann estate materials do not independently confirm the credit.

records.title: Son altesse l'amour
records.attributionNote: French-language version, Kaper credited in Jurmann's filmography

records.title: Die große Attraktion
records.attributionNote: Filmportal credits Bronislau Kaper under Musik together with Nicholas Brodszky and Walter Jurmann; Franz Grothe is credited for arrangements and Paul Dessau for musical direction. Treat Kaper's film-level music credit as confirmed, while retaining other-composer/context nuance.

records.title: Melodie der Liebe
records.attributionNote: Songs by Kaper & Jurmann: Film-Kurier premiere review (SRC0485, 27.04.1932) — 'Gesangstücke von Kaper und Jurmann'; SRC0306 lists Kinderlied, Melodie der Liebe, Schade daß Liebe ein Märchen ist, Wie gern möcht' ich dich verwöhnen, Ein Lied aus meiner Heimat as Kaper collaborations (texts Fritz Rotter). Paul Dessau: arrangement and orchestra supervision only, NOT co-composer (SRC0485). Quoted opera music: Tauber sings the Tosca aria.

records.title: Ein toller Einfall
records.attributionNote: Kaper is not treated as an on-screen score composer for the film. His confirmed contribution is at song level: 'Heut’ bin ich gut aufgelegt' (S053) and 'Ich suche Eine, die mir allein gehört' (S052), credited in sheet-music/Hofmeister sources to Walter Jurmann and B. Kaper, with text by Fritz Rotter.

records.title: Die Zwei vom Südexpreß
records.attributionNote: Filmportal credits Bronislau Kaper and Friedrich Jung under “Musik.” The official Walter Jurmann catalogue separately attributes the film’s background music and the song “Solange wir gute Freunde sind” to Kaper and Walter Jurmann. The catalogue retains both source-specific attributions rather than treating them as mutually exclusive.

records.title: Schuß im Morgengrauen
records.attributionNote: Kaper is named only by IMDb/SRC0516 in the current database evidence. SRC0166 / Weimar Talkies is contextual and does not independently confirm the composer credit. Keep this as probable, not confirmed, pending a stronger filmographic, period, archival, or music-credit source.
records.publicNote: Bronisław Kaper is currently attributed as composer with probable certainty. The positive attribution is presently based primarily on IMDb; the contextual and language-version sources linked to this record do not independently confirm the music credit.

records.title: Madame wünscht keine Kinder
records.attributionNote: Filmportal credits Bronislau Kaper and Walter Jurmann under Musik. Hans J. Salter is credited as musical director, not as an additional composer. Treat Kaper's film-level music credit as confirmed, with separate song-level evidence for the associated German and French songs.

records.title: L'Homme qui ne sait pas dire non
records.sortTitle: L'Homme qui ne sait pas dire non

records.title: Ein Lied für Dich
records.attributionNote: Filmportal credits Bronislau Kaper and Walter Jurmann under Musik; Giuseppe Verdi is also credited, and Willy Schmidt-Gentner appears under musikalische Leitung. Treat local Kaper/Jurmann credit as composer/music credit for project indexing, with Verdi and musical direction noted as source context rather than separate Kaper-work attribution.
records.publicNote: German-language feature film directed by Joe May, with music credited to Bronisław Kaper and Walter Jurmann. French-language version: Tout pour l'amour (F025).

records.title: Kind, ich freu' mich auf Dein Kommen
records.sortTitle: Kind, ich freu' mich auf Dein Kommen
records.attributionNote: Kaper and Jurmann confirmed as composers of the film's songs (SRC0134 filmportal.de; SRC0533 de.wikipedia). Their omission from some contemporary programmes and credits was a consequence of Nazi racial persecution: on 1 April 1933 the production manager Erich von Neusser ordered all personnel „nicht rein arischen Blutes“ out of the UFA studio, forcing out the Jewish director and contributors (documented via Ulrich Liebe, 1993, p. 50). Certainty upgraded uncertain→confirmed 2026-07-12.

records.title: Le greluchon délicat
records.attributionNote: Per Buxbaum/Sieghardt filmography and Unifrance/SRC0163, Pierre Candel is a printed/source music credit in this film context. Normalize as: explicit Kaper and Poterat credits retained; Pierre Candel resolved to Walter Jurmann for indexing. Do not treat P081 Pierre Candel as a real person.

records.title: Mutiny on the Bounty
records.attributionNote: Song 'Love Song of Tahiti' (m. Kaper & Jurmann, lyric Gus Kahn) — uncredited on screen; published sheet music (SRC0486) carries the printed credit. Jurmann estate list (SRC0306) also records background music for the film by Kaper & Jurmann. Score: Herbert Stothart (SRC0168; SRC0373).

records.title: Last of the Pagans
records.attributionNote: Songs 'Happy Natives' (S121) and 'Shadows on the Starlit Waters' (S122): m. Kaper & Jurmann, lyrics Ned Washington; plus background music by Kaper & Jurmann (SRC0306).

records.title: A night at the opera
records.attributionNote: Per Buxbaum/Sieghardt filmography (Walter Jurmann, Wien 2006): score by Herbert Stothart; songs by Kaper & Jurmann (incl. "Cosi Cosa"); also Nacio Herb Brown.

records.title: Two Hearts in Wax Time
records.attributionNote: Songs 'Hi-do-ho' (S127) and 'Love Needs No Inspiration' (S128) composed for this short by Jurmann in collaboration with Kaper (SRC0306); lyricist unknown. Edward Ward (SRC0401) most plausibly an MGM shorts music-department credit, not song authorship.

records.title: Trouble for Two
records.attributionNote: Not plain stock music: Jurmann estate list (SRC0306) names nine cues composed FOR this film — used: Miss Vandeleur, Second Deal, Suicide Club, The Bomb, A Trader; unused: First Deal, The Duel, The Hideout, The Next Morning — most 'in Zusammenarbeit mit Bronislaw Kaper, Franz Waxman'. Kaper co-composed original uncredited score cues with Jurmann and Waxman; credited scorer: Franz Waxman (AFI). IMDb 'stock music' label (SRC0170, reliability low) is imprecise.

records.title: We Went to College
records.attributionNote: Includes background cues

records.title: Three Smart Girls
records.attributionNote: Per Buxbaum/Sieghardt filmography (2006): Kaper & Jurmann; also Luigi Arditi.

records.title: San Francisco
records.attributionNote: Per Buxbaum/Sieghardt filmography (2006): Edward Ward and Nacio Herb Brown with Jurmann & Kaper (title song).

records.title: Man of the People
records.attributionNote: Kaper/Jurmann involvement is confirmed at song level, not as film score. SRC0306 associates Magic, Rhumba, and Tahiti with Man of the People and credits Walter Jurmann and Bronislaw Kaper. SRC0306 also notes that Rhumba and Tahiti were composed for the film but not used; Magic carries no unused annotation. Keep any manuscript/cue-sheet verification at song level, not as an active film-level review issue.

records.title: Wings of the morning
records.attributionNote: Kaper/Jurmann are not treated as score composers for Wings of the Morning. Their connection is limited to quoted/borrowed uncredited music: IMDb/SRC0173 identifies 'Marche Militaire' from Les Nuits moscovites, music by Bronislau Kaper and Walter Jurmann. AFI/SRC0481 remains the filmographic authority and credits Arthur Benjamin as score composer and Muir Mathieson as music director.
records.publicNote: Marche militaire from Les nuits moscovites

records.title: A Day at the Races
records.attributionNote: Kaper/Jurmann involvement is confirmed as song contribution, not film score. Press source SRC0114 gives music by Bronislaw Kaper and Walter Jurmann and lyrics by Gus Kahn in A Day at the Races publicity/credits context; multiple song records and relations document Kaper/Jurmann songs associated with the film. Treat Franz Waxman as score-context composer and Kaper/Jurmann as songwriters for the film's songs.

records.title: Maytime
records.attributionNote: Per Buxbaum/Sieghardt filmography (2006): score by Sigmund Romberg with an adaptation of Tchaikovsky's Fifth Symphony; Kaper & Jurmann also credited.

records.title: Everybody Sing
records.attributionNote: Per Buxbaum/Sieghardt filmography (2006): music by Kaper & Jurmann with Harry Ruby and Roger Edens.

records.title: The Spy Ring
records.attributionNote: Kaper is not treated as score composer or songwriter for The Spy Ring. The remaining association is a stock/background-music context carried by Buxbaum/Sieghardt (SRC0373), while AFI/SRC0482 is the filmographic authority and does not provide a dedicated Kaper music credit. The stale IMDb-only source ID SRC0175 was removed from the film source list because no corresponding Sources record is present.

records.title: The Adventures of Huckleberry Finn
records.attributionNote: Kaper/Jurmann involvement is confirmed at song level, not as film score. SRC0280 / CCE 1939 documents 'At night' from Huckleberry Finn, credited to Franz Waxman, Bronislaw Kaper, and Walter Jurmann. AFI/SRC0176 credits Franz Waxman for the film score. Treat Waxman as score composer and Kaper/Jurmann as song/contribution collaborators for 'At night'.

records.title: Birthright
records.publicNote: All God's Chillun Got Rhythm from A Day at the Races

records.title: Little Boy Blue
records.attributionNote: Per Buxbaum/Sieghardt filmography (2006), entry 47: MGM one-reel miniature short, 1936; producer Jack Chertok, director Harold S. Bucquet; screenplay Roy James after a poem by Eugene Field. Music by Kaper & Jurmann. Cast incl. Billy Bletcher, Charles "Chic" Sale, E.E. Clive, Scotty Beckett, Daniel L. Haynes.

records.title: Un coup de rouge
records.attributionNote: Per Buxbaum/Sieghardt filmography (2006), entry 51: France, 1937; director Gaston Roudès; based on a revue by René Dorin & Saint-Granier. Music by Kaper & Jurmann with Max d'Yreane, Vincent Scotti, Gaston Claret, Mireille and others.

records.title: Balalaika
records.attributionNote: Bronisław Kaper's documented connection with Balalaika is the song "My heart is a gypsy" / "My heart is a Gypsy" (words Gus Kahn, music Bronisław Kaper), per Catalog of Copyright Entries 1939 (SRC0281). Treat as a song contribution associated with the film, not as a Kaper score credit. The film score/adaptation credit should remain separate and requires its own filmographic source if used.

records.title: Coup de feu à l’aube
records.attributionNote: The film is a confirmed French-language version of Schuß im Morgengrauen. No direct source currently identifies Bronisław Kaper as composer or confirms reuse of his music in the French version. Do not treat the language-version relationship as a music credit.
records.publicNote: Confirmed French-language version of Schuß im Morgengrauen (F015). No direct source currently confirms Bronisław Kaper’s musical involvement in this version. The record is included for documented film-history and language-version context and must not be presented as a confirmed Kaper music credit.
